claims.head: The Penguins are likely to drive the play
claims.body: At 5-on-5, the Penguins have been near the top of the league at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Maple Leafs one of the worst. The ice is likely to tilt the Penguins’ way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

claims.body: The Penguins wait for good looks, but the Maple Leafs settle for hopeful ones. Pittsburgh is one of the league’s best for shot quality, and Toronto is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. The more dangerous chances are likely to be the Penguins’.

notes.text: Chris Tanev is out (lower-body injury), reported after he played in their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters.

Nick Blankenburg is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 15 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Troy Stecher has taken his spot beside Oliver Ekman-Larsson. That pair has had 51% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 76:24 together, about what it had with Blankenburg (48%).
Jack Roslovic is out (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-six forward. Nick Paul has taken his spot beside Auston Matthews and Easton Cowan.
Kirill Marchenko returned in their last game after missing 12 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Aatu Räty was added to the roster on Nov 23 and has played beside William Nylander and Dakota Joshua.
Oliver Ekman-Larsson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 31% of the team’s shorthanded time in 26 games, up from 6% last season.
Egor Chinakhov is on injured reserve and has missed the last 2 games.

Bryan Rust is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 15 games. Tommy Novak has taken his spot beside Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell. That line has had 53% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 99:40 together, up from 43% with Rust.
Atley Calvert was added to the roster on Nov 27 and has played beside Connor Dewar and Blake Lizotte.
Ilya Solovyov has started killing penalties: on the ice for 43% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, up from 5% last season.
Nick Robertson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 20 games, up from 2% with his old team last season.

PIT.head: The Penguins have a lot going for them
PIT.body: Pittsburgh has been out-chancing opponents lately and has home-ice advantage, while Toronto will be without Tanev. The Maple Leafs can make it interesting if their power play gets going.

TOR.head: The Maple Leafs have a hill to climb
TOR.body: Pittsburgh has been out-chancing opponents lately and has home-ice advantage, while Toronto will be without Tanev. The Maple Leafs’ best way through is a power play that gets going.

story.head: Crosby’s favorite opponent
paras: The Penguins (8-15-2) beat Buffalo 6-3 last night, and the Maple Leafs have won two in a row. Both teams are near the bottom of the standings. Going in, the Maple Leafs are last in the Atlantic (tied for 25th in the NHL) and the Pens last in the Metropolitan (31st).

The Maple Leafs have played better than their record (.426) says: their chances are worth about .493, mostly because they’re 3-10 in one-goal games. So have the Penguins (.360 on chances worth .531), mostly because they’re 4-8 in one-goal games.

The Maple Leafs get their shots through better than anyone (1st), but take more penalties than they draw (30th). They also take a lot of low-quality shots (31st), so the Penguins wait for good looks, but they settle for hopeful ones. On the other side, the Penguins sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (lowest), get more of their shots from in close than anyone (1st) and rarely throw hits (lowest). The Penguins are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Maple Leafs.

Auston Matthews (14 G / 20 A / 34 P in 27 GP) leads the Maple Leafs in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL. William Nylander (11 G / 14 A / 25 P in 27 GP) is next in line, with a point in six straight games against Pittsburgh. For the Penguins, Evgeni Malkin (8 G / 14 A / 22 P in 21 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Tommy Novak (9 G / 9 A / 18 P in 25 GP) has a team-high nine goals.

Sergei Bobrovsky (3-9-2 / .873 SV% in 14 GS) will likely start for Toronto. Pittsburgh has two options in net: Sergei Murashov (3-6-1 / .889 SV% in 10 GS) and Artūrs Šilovs (5-9-1 / .873 SV% in 15 GS). They have split the last ten starts, and Murashov got the last one last night. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
The Penguins usually control more of the chances than the Maple Leafs do.

items.text: Sidney Crosby has a point in seven straight games against Toronto.

The Maple Leafs are newly without Chris Tanev and Jack Roslovic, and have been without Nick Blankenburg since Oct 22. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Mammoth and the Avalanche are missing more right now.
The Penguins are newly without Egor Chinakhov, and have been without Bryan Rust since Oct 19.
Nick Paul has one goal on chances worth about 4.8 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
